messages.subject: Debugging Observers
parts:
Somewhat of a dupe of my earlier post.

I'm getting errors in my code in observers.  I can see that errors happen because a message gets printed, but:

1) shiny doesn't stop, so I can't traceback them,  
2) The observer bodies don't have names, so I can't debug them, and 
3) shiny catches the errors so I can't options(error=browser) them, and 
4) I can't tell which observer they are happening in for a mix of the above reasons.

Any recommendations?  can I turn off shiny's error? can I trap uncaught errors? is there a magic switch?

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Debugging Observers
parts:
Our behavior is pretty broken here. For now I'd recommend you wrap the observer bodies with your own boilerplate (or abstract it into your own version of observe) and catch the errors.

origObserve <- observe
observe <- function(expr) {
  func <- exprToFunction(expr)
  label <- deparse(body(func))

  origObserve({
    tryCatch(
      func(),
      error = function(e) {
        cat('Error:', geterrmessage(), '\n', paste(label, collapse='\n'), '\n', file=stderr())
      }
    )
  })
}

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    input$foo

    stop('BOOM')
  })
})

The above prints:

Error: BOOM 
 {
    input$foo
    stop("BOOM")
}
